text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PROD redis-primary (us-west-2) - maxclients threshold breached (connected_clients ~ 13400, configured maxclients=10000). Error rate rising for cache-layer timeouts. Impact: some user searches 503 / timeouts.

pagerduty: triggered on service=prod-redis-acceptqueue, alert=pager:redis-maxclients, runbook=/runbooks/redis-acceptqueue.md

sam c: acked on PagerDuty :hand: i'm on it, will start triage.

jess t: +1 reading metrics now — seeing acceptqueue climb, many WAIT and `ERR max number of clients reached` in redis logs.

marta k: customer-facing note? Should we throttle ingest or switch to readonly fallback?

david (db): quick note: pgbouncer -> postgres looks fine, this is pure redis connection saturation. Could be a client leak or traffic spike.

sam c: ops plan: 1) identify top client IPs by connection count 2) temporarily increase redis maxclients (short term) 3) enable acceptqueue backpressure/route to fallback cache tier 4) start controlled restart of a subset of clients with `CLIENT KILL` if needed.

jess t: running command to list client addr counts:
```
redis-cli -h redis-prod -p 6379 CLIENT LIST | awk -F 'addr=' '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -20
```
Got a few IPs with ~2k connections each from a worker pool in eu-west.

marta k: dj-analytics batch job kicked off at 14:02 UTC, might be the culprit. Paging infra to block or rate-limit that job?

sam c: I'm going to escalate to infra team and add a temporary iptables rule to the client gateway to drop excessive connections from that pool. Doing graceful steps first.

pagerduty: escalation: paging david (db) and marta k for assistance.

david (db): oncall here. If the job is misbehaving we should throttle it. I can coordinate with jobs service to pause/scale it down. Meanwhile, small config bump: `maxclients=15000` applied to replica set via config reload. This will give breathing room for mitigation.

jess t: applied `CONFIG SET maxclients 15000` on primaries, confirm connections now at 13.4k -> hold steady. Latency receded a bit.

marta k: queued a hold on dj-analytics job (paused). Noted backlog; will resume at reduced parallelism after we finish.

sam c: good. next: prune stale connections and block abusive clients. Using `CLIENT KILL` with `skipme yes` filter to target ip ranges:
```
# kill high-conn clients in a safe manner
redis-cli -h redis-prod --scan --pattern '*' | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli CLIENT KILL addr 10.20.30.*
```
Will be careful, doing small batches.

jess t: also enabled `accepting-queue-throttle` flag on the proxy tier to limit new connections per-second.

incident-bot: note added to thread: mitigation change - increased maxclients, paused batch job, started connection pruning.

david (db): rolling restart of 1 replica applied to flush problematic clients. Observing connections drop ~800 after restart. Error rates < 1% now.

sam c: customer impact: partial failures for search pages between 14:01-14:10 UTC for ~3% of requests in us-west-2. CS notified with short blurb.

marta k: wrote interim status update to status.redwood.ai: "Experiencing elevated Redis connection usage causing intermittent search errors in us-west-2. We paused a large job and applied mitigations; customers may see degraded search performance. Investigating root cause."

jess t: metrics check: acceptqueue length back to normal, avg command latency normalized, no new IP spikes.

sam c: next steps: 1) schedule postmortem, 2) patch job to use connection pool multiplexing or backoff, 3) consider connection rate-limits on gateway.

david (db): agree. I'll own postmortem and add a remediation item: circuit-breaker on high-concurrency clients + alert refinement to include client-ip topN.

sam c: handing off to next on-call (marta k) at 14:30 UTC. Leaving runbook notes and commands used in the channel.

marta k: ack taking over. will follow up on postmortem and coordinate with analytics team. Thanks all :heart: 

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved (auto-resolve) — incident marked mitigated by sam c.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook update suggestion: add a step for adding temporary `maxclients` bump and the risks (memory/perf) plus a checklist for safe `CLIENT KILL` batches.

sam c: closing thread, will file incident in postmortems/ with timeline and relevant logs.
